chunks: And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Surely, the Almighty and Glorified Allah has freed slaves from the Fire every night of the month of Ramadan, except for one who breaks his fast with an intoxicant. And when it is the last night of it, He frees in it as many as He freed in all of them.
ai.seo_question: How many people are freed from Hellfire every night of Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be him) highlights the unique divine generosity in Ramadan, where Allah liberates souls from the Fire every night, excluding only those who consume intoxicants. This tradition, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, underscores the cumulative reward of consistent devotion, culminating in a doubling of freed souls on the final night, which many scholars associate with Laylat al-Qadr or the completion of the month's spiritual journey.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 6.  It is narrated that Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) said, “Surely, the Almighty  Allah  frees  a  large  number  of  people  on  every night   of   the   month   of   Ramadan.   However   one   who concludes  his  fast  with  an intoxicant won’t be  freed. The number  of  people  freed  in  one  night  of  the  month  of 2 Surah Momin 40:60 Ramadan is equal to the number of people freed in all the past nights.”
